outcome: An immutable, network-isolated backup copy that regular restore testing proves will actually recover data.
overview: Bank backup estates are usually sized for a backup window that stopped fitting years ago, and the recovery half is rarely tested because testing requires the same window. PowerProtect with a Cyber Recovery vault addresses both halves and adds the one that matters most after a ransomware event: an immutable copy held in an isolated vault whose network path is closed except during synchronisation. The claim that deserves scrutiny is recovery time, and the only honest evidence for it is a tested restore rather than a backup success rate.

benefits.text: An immutable copy is held in a vault whose network path is closed except during synchronisation
benefits.limits: Isolation protects the copy; it does not protect against restoring compromised data, which is why the vault includes analysis rather than storage alone

benefits.text: Deduplication reduces the capacity and the backup window for the same protected data
benefits.limits: Sized from measured capacity and performance data; a design built on invoice history or on projected growth alone produces a quotation rather than an architecture

benefits.text: Restore can be tested without consuming the production backup window
benefits.limits: Testing capability is not testing practice; a restore test that is possible and never scheduled leaves the recovery claim unevidenced

residency: Backup and vault copies remain on bank-owned equipment inside the bank’s own facilities

notFor.situation: An estate already running an isolated immutable vault with tested restores
notFor.why: The capability exists; a second platform duplicates the vault without improving the tested position

notFor.situation: A buyer who will fund the vault but not the restore testing
notFor.why: An untested vault is a storage cost with an unverified recovery claim attached

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Dell implementation partner · Duration: 10–14 weeks to a vault with a first tested restore per critical tier
Support model: Vendor hardware and software support with a replacement term matched to recovery criticality; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed restore testing.
1) Assessment — protection inventory, measured change rate, stated objectives per tier, current restore evidence
2) Design — copy set for the vault, synchronisation window, analysis policy and test schedule
3) Build — protection target and isolated vault deployed and validated
4) Test and hand over — first restore tested per critical tier, schedule handed over
deliverables: The vault network path is demonstrably closed outside the synchronisation window
A restore from the vault completes within the stated objective for each critical tier
Copy analysis runs on vaulted copies and its findings are reviewable
effort: 10–14 weeks to a vault with a first tested restore per critical tier
